answer_1.quote: We propose a novel MDS framework called SgSum which formulates the MDS task as a sub-graph selection problem.
answer_1.outputs: extractive summaries in the form of sub-graphs

answer_2.quote: The summarization quality is evaluated using ROUGE F1. We report unigram and bigram overlap (ROUGE-1 and ROUGE-2) between system summaries and gold references as a means of assessing informativeness, and the longest common subsequence (ROUGE-L) as a means of accessing fluency.

answer_4.quote: In addition to the automatic evaluation, we also assess system performance by human evaluation. We use the DUC2004 as human evaluation set, and invite 2 annotators to assess the outputs of different models independently.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators assess the overall quality of summaries by ranking them considering the following criteria: (1) Informativeness: is the main meaning expressed in the source documents preserved in the summary? (2) Coherence: is the summary coherent between sentences and well-formed?
